hero.headline: Chandigarh Online MBA in Banking and Insurance: Syllabus, Fees and Career Outcomes
hero.sub: UGC-DEB approved 2-year programme with Harvard and PwC certification options

sections.tldr: One of the few online MBAs carrying a banking-specific label, covering merchant banking, banking law, treasury and risk, corporate insurance and portfolio management. Chandigarh University, NIRF Management rank 32, NAAC A+. Rs 1,65,000 after the 25% early-bird scholarship. Built for people already inside a bank or insurer.

about.body:
If you work in a bank, you have probably found that a general finance MBA teaches you things you already know and skips the things you deal with daily. This specialisation is pointed at the second category.

The subjects are Merchant Banking and Financial Services, Legal Aspect of Banking, Treasury and Risk Management, Corporate Insurance Management, Mutual Funds and Portfolio Management, and Banking and Insurance Management.

Legal Aspect of Banking is the one that earns its place. Banking is a business conducted inside a legal framework, and most costly mistakes in it are legal rather than commercial. Very few online MBAs teach it as a dedicated subject.

One thing to be clear about before you enrol: a degree does not move you up a scale on its own. Your bank's promotion policy decides whether a postgraduate qualification carries weight, and that document is the one to read first. Ask HR for the current circular.

Two things are common to every Chandigarh specialisation and worth pricing separately from the subject list. AI for Managers appears in all of them, so the AI exposure is not unique to the technical tracks. And the programme runs in two tiers, where the higher tier bundles PwC co-taught modules and additional certification. Ask which tier your fee quote covers, because the subject list does not change between them.

Chandigarh University's NAAC A+ accreditation cycle carried a validity date of September 2026, so confirm the current grade at naac.gov.in before you rely on it.

Fees quoted here are indicative and change between intakes. Confirm the current figure, which tier it buys, the early-bird terms and what sits outside the tuition with the university in writing before you pay.

syllabus.note: Sem 1-2 shared core subjects across all Chandigarh MBA specialisations. See the main Chandigarh Online MBA page for core subject list.

subjects.name: Strategy, Business and Globalization
subjects.desc: Banking strategy and competitive positioning in India's consolidating financial services sector.

subjects.name: Decision Science
subjects.desc: Statistical models for credit risk assessment, insurance pricing, and financial data analysis.

subjects.name: Merchant Banking and Financial Services
subjects.desc: Investment banking operations, IPO management, SEBI regulations, and capital market services.

subjects.name: Legal Aspect of Banking
subjects.desc: Negotiable Instruments Act, banking law, RBI guidelines, IBC provisions, and enforcement of security.

subjects.name: Treasury and Risk Management
subjects.desc: ALM, interest rate risk, FX exposure hedging, liquidity management, and Basel capital adequacy.

subjects.name: Corporate Insurance Management
subjects.desc: Life and non-life insurance products, reinsurance, IRDAI regulations, and corporate risk placement.

subjects.name: Project Management
subjects.desc: Managing banking product launches, branch rollouts, and compliance implementation projects.

subjects.name: AI for Managers
subjects.desc: AI in credit underwriting, fraud detection, regulatory reporting automation, and chatbot banking.

subjects.name: Mutual Funds and Portfolio Management
subjects.desc: Mutual fund structure, scheme types, NAV calculation, SEBI regulations, and investor advisory basics.

subjects.name: Banking and Insurance Management
subjects.desc: Commercial bank management, bancassurance, IRDA compliance, and cross-selling frameworks.

subjects.name: Capstone Project II
subjects.desc: Applied banking or insurance management project on a real financial services challenge.

whoHires.body:
This Banking and Insurance MBA syllabus maps to the following India's formal financial services sector:

**Industries:** Commercial banking, NBFCs, insurance companies, mutual fund AMCs, stock broking, treasury departments, and banking regulatory bodies

**Entry-level roles:** Banking Officer, Insurance Underwriter, Mutual Fund Analyst, Treasury Executive, Credit Officer, Relationship Manager

**Mid-level roles (3-5 years experience):** Branch Manager, Treasury Manager, Insurance Product Manager, Mutual Fund Relationship Manager, Credit Risk Manager

**Senior roles (7+ years):** Zonal Head (banking), VP Risk, Chief Underwriting Officer, Head of Treasury, Regional Head (insurance)

**Where to verify placement claims:** ask Chandigarh University for its most recent placement report, in writing, covering your specific programme and mode. Online cohorts are often reported separately from on-campus ones, or not at all. EdifyEdu does not publish employer lists we cannot source, so treat the roles above as the job families this syllabus maps to, not as a record of who has hired from this cohort.

skills.body:
The outcome is being able to hold a conversation across the bank rather than only inside your own function.

Treasury and Risk Management covers asset and liability management, liquidity and the interest rate exposure that sits under every balance sheet. Merchant Banking and Financial Services covers issue management, advisory and the fee-based side of banking that branch roles rarely see.

Mutual Funds and Portfolio Management gives you the product knowledge for wealth and advisory conversations, including how a portfolio is constructed and what risk-adjusted return actually means.

Corporate Insurance Management covers commercial lines, underwriting logic and claims, which is the bridge into bancassurance work. Legal Aspect of Banking covers recovery, security interests, negotiable instruments and the statutory duties that bound what you can agree to.

comparisons.body:
Comparing Chandigarh Online MBA Banking and Insurance against peer programmes:

**vs NMIMS Online MBA Finance:** NMIMS Finance carries the strongest brand in BFSI hiring, particularly for Mumbai-area banks and AMCs. Fee is higher at Rs 2,05,000-2,10,000. For candidates targeting Mumbai BFSI roles, NMIMS brand premium exists. CU is the better value choice at Rs 1,65,000 with PwC Financial Services content (Tier 2) for North India banking and insurance roles.

**vs Amity Online MBA Finance (Banking track):** Amity's Finance programme covers banking content but does not offer a dedicated Banking and Insurance specialisation at this depth. CU's dedicated BFSI programme with Treasury, Insurance, and Merchant Banking subjects is more aligned for BFSI career tracks.

**vs LPU Online MBA Finance:** LPU is NAAC A++ at a lower fee. CU's advantage is NIRF Management rank 32, dedicated Banking and Insurance curriculum depth, PwC Financial Services advisory content (Tier 2), and NAAC A+ credential strength for PSU banking applications where NIRF rank is sometimes a filter.

fees.body:
The Chandigarh University Online MBA in Banking and Insurance offers 2 program tiers based on certification bundle:

**Tier 1 (Primary) - Standard with Harvard ManageMentor Certificate**:
- Actual program fee: Rs 2,20,000
- 25% Early Bird Scholarship: Rs 1,65,000 net payable (Rs 55,000 savings)
- Payment options:
  - Annual: Rs 82,500 per year x 2 years
  - Semester-wise: Rs 41,250 per semester x 4 semesters
  - Full upfront: Rs 1,65,000 one-time
- Included certification: Harvard Business Publishing certificate

**Tier 2 (Premium Upgrade) - 3-Certificate Bundle**:
- Actual program fee: Rs 2,20,000 (same base fee)
- 18% Early Bird Scholarship: Rs 1,80,400 net payable (Rs 39,600 savings)
- Payment options:
  - Annual: Rs 90,200 per year x 2 years
  - Semester-wise: Rs 45,100 per semester x 4 semesters
  - Full upfront: Rs 1,80,400 one-time
- Included certifications (3):
  1. PwC co-created and co-taught MBA modules (unmatched in India)
  2. CAPM (Certified Associate in Project Management) certification preparation
  3. Harvard Business Publishing certificate

**Additional charges (both tiers)**:
- Registration fee: Rs 1,000 (one-time, non-refundable)

**Zero-cost EMI**: Available directly through Chandigarh University (no external marketing partner or NBFC intermediary, a differentiator among Indian online MBAs). Contact our counsellor for current tenure options (6, 12, 18, or 24 months).

**Early Bird Scholarship terms**: Availability varies by admission cycle. The 25% Tier 1 scholarship and 18% Tier 2 scholarship are currently active but subject to timing. Reconfirm eligibility with our counsellor before enrolment.

EdifyEdu reconfirms fees with Chandigarh University each quarter. Please reconfirm current tier options, Early Bird eligibility, and fees with our counsellor before any payment. Fees listed are indicative.

For a full programme review and fee comparison, see our [CU Online MBA fees and honest review](/blog/chandigarh-university-online-mba-review).

certificate.body:
Graduates receive a Chandigarh University MBA degree certificate with Banking and Insurance noted on the marksheet, issued under UGC-DEB 2020 standards. NIRF Management rank 32 and NAAC A+ credentials are recognised by banks, insurance companies, AMCs, and NBFCs.

Tier 1 graduates receive the Harvard Business Publishing certificate. Tier 2 graduates additionally receive PwC Financial Services advisory co-teaching acknowledgement and CAPM certification preparation, strengthening profiles for banking advisory, risk management, and insurance product roles. DigiLocker verification is available.

faqs.question: What is the PwC partnership in Chandigarh Online MBA?
faqs.answer: Chandigarh University's premium tier includes full MBA modules co-created and co-taught by PwC industry experts. This is unmatched among Indian online MBAs - most offer only generic curriculum. PwC-taught modules are particularly valuable for Banking and Insurance professionals seeking roles at Big 4 BFSI advisory, risk management consulting, or senior positions at banks and insurance companies that partner with PwC. The PwC partnership is included in Tier 2 (premium) at Rs 1,80,400 net.

faqs.question: What is the difference between Tier 1 and Tier 2 fee options?
faqs.answer: Both tiers share the same Rs 2,20,000 base fee and identical curriculum. Tier 1 applies a 25% Early Bird Scholarship at Rs 1,65,000 net with the Harvard Business Publishing certificate. Tier 2 applies an 18% Early Bird Scholarship at Rs 1,80,400 net with three certifications: Harvard, CAPM preparation, and PwC co-taught modules. For BFSI professionals targeting Big 4 advisory or senior banking roles, Tier 2 adds strong profile differentiation.

faqs.question: Is zero-cost EMI really available directly through Chandigarh University?
faqs.answer: Yes. Chandigarh University offers zero-cost EMI through the university's own payment infrastructure, not through an NBFC or external marketing partner. Tenures of 6, 12, 18, and 24 months are typically available. Confirm current tenure options with our counsellor before enrolment.

faqs.question: Is this MBA useful for PSU bank promotion examinations?
faqs.answer: The Chandigarh University MBA is UGC-DEB entitled, making it valid for eligibility requirements in PSU bank promotions and lateral entry requirements that specify a management degree. The Banking and Insurance specialisation covers subjects directly aligned with banking officer promotions in areas of treasury, credit, and regulatory compliance. Always verify the specific promotion examination eligibility criteria as requirements vary by bank and cadre.

faqs.question: Does the MBA cover insurance regulatory aspects (IRDAI)?
faqs.answer: Yes. Corporate Insurance Management in Sem 3 covers IRDAI product regulations, insurance contract law, reinsurance, and corporate risk placement. Banking and Insurance Management in Sem 4 covers bancassurance regulatory requirements and insurance distribution compliance. For insurance professionals, this provides the management credential with regulatory grounding. For deeper insurance actuarial knowledge, supplementary FIII or AIIF examinations would be needed alongside the MBA.

chooseIf: You work in banking, NBFC, insurance, or AMC and want a NAAC A+ NIRF #19 credential at Rs 1,65,000.
You want PwC Financial Services advisory content (Tier 2) for banking risk, treasury, or insurance roles.
You are in North India's BFSI sector and want strong regional employer recognition.
You prefer zero-cost EMI directly through the university.
consider: You specifically need NMIMS brand for Mumbai-based BFSI hiring - NMIMS carries a stronger brand premium there.
You are targeting IIM or Tier-1 brand for management consulting in BFSI.
Your budget is under Rs 1.2 lakh and LPU NAAC A++ at lower fee is acceptable.
